overview: White plays 3.g4 after 2.Bf4 e6, offering the g-pawn to open the g-file and chase the f5 pawn. Black can take with ...fxg4 and has a safe extra pawn, while White hopes for Qd2, Nc3 and h3 plus rapid development. The theory is thin, so the evidence is kept short.

white_ideas.idea: Open the h- and g-files with h3 and develop with Nc3 and Qd2
Use the f4 bishop and the weak e5 square

typical_structures.structure: Open kingside files after g-pawn trade; central pawns undecided

character.notes: An early kingside pawn offer, concrete and double-edged.

gambit.notes: White's g4 pawn can be taken with ...fxg4.

structure.notes: Flexible as the centre is not fixed.

character.reason: Early pawn offer and open lines against the king.

gambit.reason: White gives the g-pawn, Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Kingside pawn offer with little development behind it.

structure.reason: The centre remains undecided while the g-file opens.

plans.reason: White offers the pawn for open lines and quicker development against Black's king.
